rawContent: #MeToo has given so many people the space to come forward. It also has given institutions a chance to learn to respond differently. Watching this closely.

We all have to reckon with the institutions that allow this sort of conduct to go unaddressed. Speaking tours, book deals, interviews are not the answer. #MeToo A Comeback but No Reckoning https://t.co/i7lpWdmYWO

Grateful to you for this reporting—which shows us that the Department & @BetsyDeVosED are leaning into worst instincts and somehow ignoring the most vibrant movement around harassment and violence in a generation. #MeToo #HandsOffIX

I don’t want to hear another word about her dress. I only want to hear from the many people who didn’t stop those inappropriate hands and words in real time. How many women have had this moment? Done. #MeToo #ArethaFrankinFuneral
“I’m hear to say to you black women and girls, that you deserve safety and you deserve protection. And I’ve committed my life to ensuring that you have it.” Thank you @TaranaBurke #MeToo

I just don’t understand why they won’t do a serious investigation. I really don’t. It’s been 3 days since we heard from Dr. Ford, her life has been turned upside down. She is asking for a serious process. We owe it to her. We owe it to the many others who are saying #MeToo⁠ ⁠

Dr. Blasey Ford is willing to testify. She is not asking for a lot, she is seeking conditions that will be fair & allow her to be safe. We owe it to her. We owe it to all survivors. We are with you. @ChuckGrassley this is your time to get it right. #MeToo  https://t.co/Id8858mA30
This is why Dr Blasey Ford made the reasonable request to have a fair and safe process. The Rs again and again are showing they do not take these very credible allegations seriously. #MeToo
Today’s hearing is happening in the midst of the #MeToo in the midst of #TIMESUP. Dr. Ford is not alone. She is with the millions of survivors and allies who are saying #TIMESUP
It was also before #MeToo went viral, and before there were examples of women being believed, even when they name their experiences with powerful men.

Tonight, someone asked me where I find hope. I put my hope in the thousands of people who waged this fight, week after week. I put my hope in the many women led organizations who are fueling this movement. I put my hope in the millions of people who said #MeToo

On this #MeToo anniversary there is one thing I have been reminded of again and again over the last year: People who we love and admire and who have done great things in the world can also abuse their power. https://t.co/Q7XI9J6Xpt

Ok to acknowledge both. In fact that’s how we will finally progress-by acknowledging that there is no one type of abuser and no one type of victim. It is complicated and the millions who said #MeToo  demonstrate that point.
#AnitaHill-if our government won’t ensure that we can work free of harassment then our industry must do it. Wise words on the #MeToo Anniversary. #EllleWomeninHollywood https://t.co/1l7UV9BtVh
What’s next? A strategy for healing. #MeToo https://t.co/NqzDv7FSNy
DearWorld: By 2020, we need to see at least 20 states pass laws that strengthen legal protections against sexual violence and harassment. #metoo https://t.co/2WVpbRpqX3
We can get there—#MeToo has revealed the many ways harassment and violence plagues people. Our institutions must respond.

It won’t be easy, but we CAN give the next generation the kinds of communities, schools, and workplaces they deserve, free from sexual violence or harassment. #DearWorld #metoo https://t.co/2WVpbRpqX3 https://t.co/RczEkp1xbO
Sometimes visionary leaders step up at just the right time and we are all better for it. Thank you @MonicaRamirezDC #DearSisters. #MeToo #TimesUp
